summary:
The big story this cycle is Lilly's TRANSCEND-T2D-2 topline result (Oct 28, 2026). It's the first Phase 3 head-to-head of retatrutide against semaglutide 2 mg, in 1,298 adults with type 2 diabetes on metformin, with or without an SGLT2 inhibitor, over 80 weeks. A1C fell 2.2% on retatrutide 9 mg and on 12 mg, versus 1.8% on semaglutide. Weight fell 19.5% (9 mg) and 20.9% (12 mg), versus 9.4%. These figures use the efficacy estimand. Side effects: diarrhea 28.3–32.7% vs 26.4%, nausea 21.2–23.8% vs 21.3%, vomiting 10.2–15.0% vs 13.2%. A skin-sensation side effect (dysesthesia) was reported in 4.8–6.5% vs 2.7%. Discontinuation for side effects was 4.8–7.9% vs 2.7%. The results are not yet peer-reviewed. The story is in mainstream news (Reuters, ABC, NY Post, STAT), so it is peaking. It qualifies for Lane C because it is a fresh randomized head-to-head first reported within 48 hours, but L1 10-29 already covered it and was held. The best move is to fix and re-render that video today rather than start a new one. The skin-sensation side effect is an early Short hook that almost nobody is covering yet.

Lane A has strong fresh hooks:
- **Stopping tirzepatide:** the Wales Online NHS GP warning and the Medscape piece (both Oct 28) point to a pilot RCT. In 39 adults, 4-month regain was 10.75% with usual care, 3.60% with a coaching app and 3.58% with medically tailored meals.
- **Hair loss:** Medscape (Oct 28) reports GLP-1 hair loss looks similar by race.
- **Plateau:** a 12-month real-world tirzepatide paper came out in Diabetes Obes Metab (Oct 28).
- **Bones and muscle:** the Arch Osteoporos review, a J Clin Med paper on device-estimated muscle loss, and the Omada muscle-share news.

Timely Shorts and Reels:
- **Pregnancy and breastfeeding:** ACOG's Oct 23 advisory, with WSJ pickup Oct 28. Use caution and frame it as "talk to your clinician".
- **Halloween and food noise:** Psychiatric Times (Oct 28), with Halloween on Oct 31.
- **Alcohol:** the Heineken document (Reuters Oct 27, NewsNation Oct 29). Keep the evidence wording cautious.
- **Gallbladder and pancreas:** a new propensity-matched tirzepatide comparison.
- **Gray market:** one "what's confirmed?" Short (Penn's AI analysis of Reddit posts from gray-market retatrutide users, Mashable's TikTok report).

Rejected: the $300-a-year telehealth GLP-1 angle (cost and sourcing) and anything about microdosing.

candidates.topic: Retatrutide vs semaglutide 2 mg in type 2 diabetes: TRANSCEND-T2D-2 Phase 3 head-to-head (1,298 adults on metformin ± SGLT2i, 80 weeks). A1C −2.2% (9 and 12 mg) vs −1.8%; weight −19.5%/−20.9% vs −9.4% (Lilly topline, Oct 28, 2026)
candidates.angle: Lane C long-form (re-render the held L1 10-29 with the masking and voice fixes): 'You have type 2 diabetes and you're already on metformin. What did a triple-hormone drug add?' Answer in the first 15 s. Give A1C and weight per arm, the efficacy estimand described plainly ('if everyone stayed on treatment'), and side effects for both drugs, including the 4.8–6.5% dysesthesia. Say: investigational, not approved, topline, not yet peer-reviewed. The 13:00 retatrutide Short gets a 'what's confirmed?' loop ending.
candidates.predicted_peak: 0–3 days (news peak Oct 28–30); search tail for weeks
candidates.why_now: First reported Oct 28 (Lilly press release 10:45 ET). Picked up by Reuters, ABC, NY Post, STAT, Fierce, BioSpace, Everyday Health and local TV. It meets every Lane C rule: fresh within 48 h, randomized head-to-head, named next-gen drug. EloraTZP shows this type earns about 54% of our watch time.

evidence.source: Eli Lilly press release (PR Newswire), Oct 28 2026
evidence.signal: N=1,298, 80 weeks, efficacy estimand, per-arm A1C and weight, AE rates, discontinuation 4.8–7.9% vs 2.7%
Trial registration: population and design
Mainstream consumer pickup
Trade/science press coverage

candidates.topic: Retatrutide's skin-sensation side effect (dysesthesia): 4.8–6.5% vs 2.7% on semaglutide 2 mg in TRANSCEND-T2D-2. What it is and what's known
candidates.angle: Calm 08:00 'honest uncertainty' body-worry Short: what dysesthesia means (tingling or unusual skin sensations), how often it happened in each arm, that it led some people to stop treatment, and what's still unknown. Topline only, not yet peer-reviewed. Use the exact wording 'skin-sensation side effect'.
candidates.why_now: Mainstream headlines lead on 'double the weight loss', so this side-effect detail is barely covered. People will start searching it as the trial details spread.

evidence.signal: Dysesthesia 4.8–6.5% vs 2.7%

candidates.topic: What happens when you stop tirzepatide? SURMOUNT-4 regain, plus a new pilot RCT: 4-month regain 10.75% with usual care vs 3.60% with a coaching app and 3.58% with medically tailored meals (n=39, Obes Sci Pract, Oct 7; Medscape Oct 28)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form, 'What Happens When You Stop Tirzepatide?'. Open on 'You're thinking about stopping. Here's what the trials show happens next.' Cover SURMOUNT-4 (335 vs 335 randomized at week 36, +14.0% regain from week 36 to week 88). Then the hopeful part: structured support slowed early regain in a small pilot. Label it pilot, n=39, and note it was GLP-1 drugs in general. Say 'don't stop or change your medicine on your own'.
keywords: what happens when you stop tirzepatide
how to keep weight off after stopping tirzepatide
candidates.predicted_peak: 1–3 weeks (New Year and insurance changes push stopping questions)
candidates.why_now: Fresh coverage in the last 48 h: Medscape (Oct 28), the Wales Online NHS GP warning (Oct 28), CBC (Oct 27), Grocery Dive and Food Dive on 'lapsed GLP-1 users', and CNBC on employers dropping coverage in 2027. It's third in the playbook's Lane A order and has been in our snapshots twice.

evidence.source: News-Medical on the Obesity Science & Practice pilot RCT

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and your bones and muscle: Arch Osteoporos systematic review of GLP-1 skeletal effects (Oct 23), J Clin Med device-estimated muscle loss (Oct 15) and SURMOUNT-1 body-scan substudy
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form, first in the playbook order. Answer within 15 s: about 75% of the weight lost was fat and about 25% lean (SURMOUNT-1 substudy: 160 scanned, 124 on tirzepatide vs 36 on placebo, 72 weeks; Look et al. 2025). Then what the bone review found and what's still unknown. Then protein and strength training as the practical payoff. Mention the semaglutide mouse bone result only as 'mice, not people'.
candidates.predicted_peak: steady; refreshed by news over the next 2 weeks
candidates.why_now: In 5 snapshots (momentum steady at 70–72). The bones Short got 237 views, our best body-worry result. New Oct 28 hooks: Omada members gained muscle share, plus a semaglutide bone-building signal in male mice.

evidence.signal: Skeletal effects of GLP-1 RAs in adults with overweight/obesity

Omada GLP-1 users gained muscle share

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide hair loss: how common, and does it differ by race? Medscape (Oct 28) on GLP-1 hair loss looking similar across racial groups, plus the Med Sci (Basel) skin side-effect review (Oct 9)

Start with the trial rates and the observational 'linked to' data, give the new finding that it looks similar by race, then explain the usual cause (shedding after rapid weight loss) and what helps: protein and talking to a clinician. The 08:00 Short covers the race-similarity fact.
